selected_evidence.requirement: SSH login restricted to remote-access members
selected_evidence.summary: The effective daemon policy reports `allowgroups remote-access`; member authentication succeeded, while sshd explicitly rejected a nonmember because its groups were not listed.
Both initial and final checks show `opsadmin` in the local `remote-access` group.

Evidence captures the healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered active/enabled sshd, persistent configuration and membership, successful member login, and continued nonmember rejection.
sshd is active, enabled, listening on port 22, and syntax-valid; the policy and membership remain present, and temporary credentials and the probe account are absent.

set -eu
getent group remote-access >/dev/null || groupadd remote-access
if ! getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null; then useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash opsadmin; fi
usermod -a -G remote-access opsadmin
id opsadmin
getent group remote-access

set -eu
cfg=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/01-remote-access.conf
tmp=$(mktemp /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/.remote-access.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' 'AllowGroups remote-access' > "$tmp"
chown root:root "$tmp"
chmod 0644 "$tmp"
mv "$tmp" "$cfg"
if ! /usr/sbin/sshd -t; then rm -f "$cfg"; exit 1; fi
systemctl reload sshd
systemctl is-active sshd

for n in 1 2 3 4 5; do state=$(systemctl is-active sshd 2>/dev/null || true); [ "$state" = active ] && break; sleep 1; done
/usr/sbin/sshd -t
printf 'sshd_state=%s\n' "$(systemctl is-active sshd)"
/usr/sbin/sshd -T | grep '^allowgroups '
id opsadmin
getent group remote-access
ss -ltnp '( sport = :22 )'
timeout 5 ssh-keyscan -T 3 "$NODE_IP" >/dev/null 2>&1
printf 'ssh_reachable=%s:%s\n' "$NODE_IP" 22
